one_liner: User-space multi-level block cache over SPDK SSDs that runs unmodified in-memory programs out-of-core, beating Linux swap and mmap.
what_it_does: TriCache lets an in-memory program (Ligra, RocksDB PlainTable, GNU sort, LiveGraph) process datasets larger than RAM without code changes. Large allocations and file mmaps are redirected into a virtual address range backed by NVMe SSDs; an LLVM plugin (TriCacheInstrument, TriCacheAlloc) instruments memory accesses so they go through the cache, and libcache interposes malloc/free, mmap/munmap/msync/madvise, read/write, memcpy/memset/memmove/memchr, the str* functions and pthread_create. It is configured through environment variables (CACHE_PHY_SIZE, CACHE_VIRT_SIZE, CACHE_NUM_CLIENTS, CACHE_CONFIG, CACHE_MALLOC_THRESHOLD), not through an API. A C++ header layer (cached_ptr, cached_allocator) can also be used directly.
how_it_is_fast: Address translation and concurrency control are split across levels: a per-thread (or per-fiber) direct cache and a private cache serve repeated accesses to the same page without locking, and only misses reach a shared cache partitioned across dedicated server cores, each owning SSDs through SPDK (with libaio and io_uring backends also present). It uses a compact hash page table and CLOCK/LRU replacement in user space, so no page faults or kernel page-cache locks sit on the hot path. Per the paper abstract, this exploits spatial and temporal locality to make per-access storage-to-memory translation cheap enough for a virtual-memory interface.
when_to_use: An existing in-memory C/C++ program must run on a dataset several times larger than DRAM and rewriting it for out-of-core is not an option.
Linux swap or mmap thrashes on random-access out-of-core workloads such as PageRank or WCC on large graphs, RocksDB PlainTable over mmap, or LiveGraph.
A dedicated server with many NVMe SSDs that can be handed to SPDK, plus spare cores for cache server threads.
Research or prototyping that compares against FastMap, FlashGraph or swap, where the OSDI'22 artifact scripts can be reused.
when_not_to_use: BFS-like traversals: per the paper snippet, the BFS result is 0.85x (a slowdown) in the swap/FlashGraph comparison.

Shared or production machines: the configured SSDs are reformatted repeatedly, md RAIDs on the host will be broken, and setup needs password-free sudo, unlimited memlock and transparent hugepages disabled.
Programs not built with clang: libcache and the instrumentation plugin need Clang (clang-13 in the scripts), and code that is not instrumented will not go through the cache.
Small or commodity setups: the artifact targets 2x EPYC 7742, at least 512 GB RAM and 8 SSDs; there is no evidence for laptop-scale use.
Long-term maintained dependencies: it is an artifact branch (osdi-ae) with 4 issues, one open (LiveGraph SF100 run fails, 2025-11-30).

integration.form: static lib (libcache) plus LLVM pass plugin; header-only C++ core (cache_header)
integration.dependencies: SPDK v21.04 with TriCache's patch (DPDK), Boost (fiber, thread), libnuma, libaio, optional liburing, OpenMP, bundled mimalloc and fadec
integration.min_toolchain: C++17; Clang 13 (scripts) for libcache and the plugin; CMake; built with -march=native and ThinLTO
integration.platforms: Linux x86-64 with NVMe SSDs (tested Debian 11.1, kernel 5.10)
integration.thread_safety: Designed for multithreaded programs: per-thread/per-fiber direct and private caches in front of a partitioned shared cache; pthread_create is hooked to register clients
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — no source changes, but the program must be recompiled with the Clang plugin and linked against libcache, and SSDs must be given to SPDK

gotchas: Startup throws if CACHE_PHY_SIZE, CACHE_VIRT_SIZE, CACHE_NUM_CLIENTS, CACHE_CONFIG or CACHE_MALLOC_THRESHOLD is unset; how to size them came up in issue #1.
Only allocations above CACHE_MALLOC_THRESHOLD, and mmaps above the configured file threshold, are redirected into the cache; smaller ones stay in DRAM.
libcache replaces memcpy, memset, memcmp, strlen, read, write and other libc symbols process-wide, which can interact badly with other interposers or sanitizers.
Builds use -march=native, so binaries are not portable across CPUs.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick TriCache over UMap, FastMap or vmcache when the program cannot be changed and you can recompile with Clang and give it whole SSDs. UMap needs explicit umap() regions, FastMap is a kernel patch on 4.14, and vmcache/exmap is a buffer manager you build a DBMS around. Choose SPDK or liburing directly when you control the I/O code.
verified_claims_summary: Per WebSearch snippets of the OSDI'22 paper (the PDF and the project page are egress-blocked): on uk-2014 with Ligra, TriCache's speedups 'over OS swapping and FlashGraph' are given as 6.30x and 5.31x on PageRank, 26.1x and 1.46x on WCC, and 0.85x and 2.05x on BFS; the snippet's pairing is ambiguous, so which baseline the BFS 0.85x belongs to is not certain. The snippets also report up to 12.4x over mmap for LiveGraph, 2-3 orders of magnitude over mmap for out-of-core RocksDB, and up to 39.3x over swapping for GNU sort, on 2x EPYC 7742, 512 GB RAM and 8x Intel P4618 SSDs. The repo holds the scripts to reproduce these but no result numbers.
status_note: Research artifact (osdi-ae default branch, last touched 2025-12-08 for dataset links), Apache-2.0 and reproducible with the bundled scripts, but intrusive and hardware-heavy; treat it as a reference design rather than a library to depend on.
